question: I’m 63, receiving CPP retirement benefits and working at a CPP-covered job. Can I opt out of CPP contributions now?
generated_answer:
In Canada, if you're 65 or older and receiving Canada Pension Plan (CPP) retirement benefits, you can choose to stop contributing to the CPP. However, if you're under 65, you must continue to contribute to the CPP if you're working and earning a income from a CPP-covered job.

Since you're 63 and still working, you're required to continue making CPP contributions, even though you're already receiving CPP retirement benefits. You won't be able to opt out of CPP contributions until you reach the age of 65.

It's worth noting that continuing to contribute to the CPP while receiving benefits can potentially increase your retirement benefits. The additional contributions you make will be used to calculate your Post-Retirement Benefit (PRB), which can result in a higher monthly benefit amount.

If you have any further questions or concerns, I recommend speaking with a representative from Service Canada or a financial advisor to discuss your specific situation and options.
